conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: LLM-orchestrated PET/CT agents enabled workflow-level automation from raw DICOM to quantification and structured draft reporting under real-world conditions. Although primary tumor detection was highly reliable, nodal and metastatic assessment revealed systematic limitations, supporting a collaborative role with continued expert oversight in complex clinical scenarios.

fig.cap: Prompt-driven LLM-agent orchestration for qualitative interpretation and quantitative PET/CT analysis. (A) Qualitative draft reporting. Given prompts for interpretation, LLM selects appropriate PET/CT series, generates whole-body maximum-intensity-projection (MIP) images, and invokes vision-enabled LLM (Vision-LLM) to produce structured report of abnormal [18F]FDG uptake. (B) Organ-based quantitative SUV computation. For liver SUV estimation, agent performs CT-based organ segmentation (TotalSegmentator) and computes SUV metrics, providing quantitative summaries with representative fusion images. (C) End-to-end lesion detection and reporting. For comprehensive analysis, agent coordinates AutoPET-based segmentation, visualization, and quantitative measurements (SUVmax, metabolic tumor volume [MTV], total lesion glycolysis [TLG]), followed by vision-enabled LLM–assisted structured reporting.

42595646.title: Post-therapy radioiodine imaging characterizes occult metastatic differentiated thyroid carcinoma years after thyroidectomy for presumed benign multinodular goiter.

42218056.title: The role of cardiac PET imaging in cardiac amyloidosis.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion

Over the past decade, substantial advances in quantitative imaging, detector technology, hybrid imaging, computational dosimetry, and theranostics have transformed radiation management from standardized activity administration toward increasingly individualized approaches.

42419604.title: Validation of a pan-ELastography Machine-learning (ELM) score to predict clinically significant portal hypertension in compensated advanced chronic liver disease.
42419604.authors: Giuffrè M, Kresevic S, Ravaioli F, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The ELM score outperformed the current Baveno VII criteria and substantially reduced the gray zone across elastography modalities, supporting broader and safer non-invasive identification of patients with CSPH who may benefit from non-selective beta-blocker therapy.

extras.label: Impact and implications
extras.text: Clinically significant portal hypertension is central to prognosis in compensated advanced chronic liver disease, yet current non-invasive strategies classify 40-50% of patients as indeterminate. This study introduces a pan-elastography machine-learning model that integrates liver and spleen stiffness with clinical variables to address this limitation. The results are important for hepatologists and healthcare systems because the ELM score reduced the diagnostic gray zone to ∼12% in external validation, compared with 47.9% for Baveno VII, while maintaining high rule-out and rule-in accuracy (NPV up to 0.91 and PPV up to 0.96). In practice, these findings could support earlier non-invasive identification of patients eligible for non-selective β-blocker therapy, more targeted use of HVPG in indeterminate cases, and harmonized risk stratification across elastography modalities, while recognizing that prospective validation and regulatory approval are required before routine clinical implementation.

42323021.title: MRI-based prediction of very early recurrence within 1 year after resection of HCC: An international cohort study.
42323021.authors: Wei H, Heo S, Yang Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The MERP models may serve as robust, generalizable, and biologically informed tools for predicting very early HCC recurrence and may help refine risk-stratified management strategies.

extras.label: Impact and implications
extras.text: Very early recurrence (VER) of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) within 1 year after resection reflects aggressive tumor biology and is associated with poor prognosis, yet reliable tools for predicting VER remain scarce. In this large, international, multicenter cohort of patients with a single Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage 0/A HCC undergoing curative-intent resection, we developed and externally validated two MRI-based models (MERP-pre and MERP-post) that integrate routinely available clinicopathological and imaging variables. The MERP models consistently outperformed existing prognostic systems and effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with distinct 1-year recurrence-free survival across diverse cohorts. These findings highlight the potential of the MERP models to complement existing prognostic systems and optimize risk-stratified management of HCC.

42234028.title: Virtual non-contrast images from dual-layer spectral CT: comparison with true non-contrast across abdominal structures.
42234028.authors: De Santis D, Del Gaudio A, Masci B, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: VNC cannot replace TNC based on the current evidence; further refinements are required for broader clinical adoption.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question True non-contrast images (TNC) are essential in abdominal CT, yet it remains unclear whether spectral CT-derived virtual non-contrast images (VNC) can reliably replace TNC imaging. Findings VNC images approximate TNC images but introduce consistent attenuation biases, reduced subjective quality, and altered calcification metrics, preventing full replacement of dedicated non-contrast acquisitions. Clinical relevance Replacing TNC with VNC images reduces radiation exposure, yet current VNC performance shows measurable differences from TNC, indicating that algorithmic refinement is required before routine diagnostic use in abdominal CT.

42829266.title: PSMA-PET/CT-guided Intensification of Radiation Therapy for Prostate Cancer (PSMAgRT): 5-yr Analysis of a Phase 2 Randomized Controlled Trial.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Although the primary FFS end point was not met in the overall population, treatment-effect estimates favored PSMAgRT in the high-risk and post-RP strata. These findings provide a meaningful rationale for the target populations currently being evaluated in the definitive phase 3 PATRON trial.

extras.label: Results and limitations
extras.text: Among 253 patients, median follow-up was 66 mo (range 9-91). The 5-yr primary FFS was 66% with PSMAgRT versus 62% in controls (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.80; one-sided 90% CI, upper bound 1.04; p1 = 0.14). FFBP favored PSMAgRT: 72% versus 65% overall (subdistribution HR [sHR] 0.70, one-sided 90% CI upper bound 0.92; p1 = 0.048), 81% versus 66% in patients with high-risk disease (sHR 0.54; p1 = 0.07), and 80% versus 68% in patients in post-RP stratum (sHR 0.54; p1 = 0.037). In an exploratory, post hoc analysis combining patients with high-risk disease and those in the post-RP stratum, FFBP favored PSMAgRT (sHR 0.54, 95% CI = 0.32-0.91; two-sided p = 0.02). Only one grade ≥3 event was possibly related to dose escalation. Limitations include a phase 2 design with a heterogeneous population.
