43043182.title: Histotripsy versus Established Thermal Ablation Technologies: A Comparative Analysis of FDA MAUDE Adverse Event Reporting Patterns.
43043182.authors: Kundu A, Tam A, Zhao L, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Histotripsy demonstrated higher reported frequencies of serious AEs and death in early postmarket MAUDE surveillance compared with pooled MWA/RFA; however, differences in technology maturity and reporting era may have contributed to differential AE reporting, warranting prospective evaluation.

43076674.title: Evaluation of Total Patent Branch Vessel Ostial Area at Preoperative CT Angiography for Predicting Type II Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
43076674.authors: Wang W, Zhou S, Han H, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA.

42363965.title: Do hepatic and biliary functional data from gadoxetate-enhanced MRI add value in predicting outcomes in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC)?
42363965.authors: Sandrasegaran K, Shah AS, Thompson CP, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Relative enhancement ratio of extrahepatic bile ducts at 20 min after gadoxetate disodium provides useful information in predicting adverse events in PSC patients and is complementary or superior to the currently used clinical scoring systems.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Can functional hepatic and biliary parameters, obtained from gadoxetate-enhanced MRI, be useful in predicting adverse events in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis? Findings The relative enhancement of proximal bile ducts (REPD) was useful in predicting adverse events and the need for liver transplantation within 2 years of MRI. Clinical relevance ANALI score predicts need for liver transplantation and may be included in MRI reports of patients with PSC. REPD is more difficult to measure on a routine clinical basis and may only be useful in drug trials.

42708849.title: Evaluation of Super-Resolution Contrast-enhanced US in Crohn Disease Activity Assessment.
42708849.authors: Aihemaiti S, Li M, Xu M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: SRCEUS demonstrated excellent performance in differentiating CD activity through high-resolution depiction of microstructural changes, with superior performance to conventional CEUS.

42708850.title: Improving Recognition Performance and Reader Efficiency for Femoral-Neck Fracture Detection on Pelvic or Hip Radiographs Using Artificial Intelligence.
42708850.authors: Lin XX, Qian YR, Zhou SH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: OccuNet demonstrated excellent performance for femoral-neck fracture detection on pelvic or hip radiographs, maintained high sensitivity in radiograph-negative or indeterminate (Garden I-II) fractures, and improved reader sensitivity and efficiency.

42808899.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Bosniak v2019 for Predicting Cancer and Unfavorable Histology in Class III-IV Cystic Renal Masses.
42808899.authors: Tse JR, Khalatbari S, Yosef M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Bosniak v2019 helps predict cancer and cancer with unfavorable histologic features. Nodule size was strongly associated with unfavorable histologic features.

42398521.title: Somatostatin receptor PET response assessment framework for patients with neuroendocrine tumours (V1.0): a modified Delphi consensus from the European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society (endorsed by EANM and NANETS).
42398521.authors: Deroose CM, Leupe H, Hicks RJ, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Somatostatin receptor PET imaging is integral to the management of patients with neuroendocrine tumours (NETs), yet standardised criteria for therapy response assessment with the use of this modality are not available. This Policy Review reports the development of the European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society somatostatin receptor PET response assessment framework, established through a structured modified Delphi process coordinated by the European Neuroendocrine Tumor Society.

42744522.title: Advances in the imaging of liver cancer.
42744522.authors: Joo I, Lee JM, Ronot M

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Liver cancer remains a major global health burden, with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) accounting for the vast majority of primary liver malignancies. As most patients are diagnosed at advanced stages, imaging plays a central role across the entire care continuum - from surveillance and early detection to diagnosis, staging, prognostic stratification, and treatment response assessment.

42685984.title: Emerging strategies for hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance: Abbreviated MRI, biomarkers and benefit stratification.
42685984.authors: Ioannou GN, Jepsen P, Rowe IA

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance with semi-annual ultrasound and alpha-fetoprotein is recommended in clinical practice guidelines for patients with cirrhosis and selected patients with chronic hepatitis B. However, this strategy has suboptimal sensitivity for early-stage HCC and poor real-world adherence; moreover, randomised trial evidence demonstrating reduced HCC-related or all-cause mortality in patients with cirrhosis is lacking.

42301015.title: Radiology Reimagined: Interoperability and Lessons Learned from the Imaging AI in Practice Demonstration.
42301015.authors: Jiao A, Hussain M, Sippel Schmidt T, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: The Radiology Reimagined demonstration, formerly known as Imaging AI in Practice, is presented at the Radiological Society of North America (RSNA) Annual Meeting. It highlights how interoperability and semantic standards can facilitate the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into radiology workflows.

42836752.title: Standardizing Liver MR Elastography: Guidelines for Reliable Stiffness Measurement in Chronic Liver Disease.
42836752.authors: Serai SD, Pepin K, Chen J, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: MR elastography provides the noninvasive, repeatable, and reproducible quantitative biomarker of liver stiffness for the assessment of fibrosis in chronic liver disease. However, variability in image acquisition, reconstruction, and analysis across scanners and institutions can limit measurement repeatability and reproducibility.

42678260.title: Convergence of Local and Systemic Therapies: A Comprehensive Society of Interventional Oncology Framework for 90Y Radioembolization with Immunotherapy in HCC.
42678260.authors: Avritscher R, Kim E, Chew V, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Combination approaches using systemic immunotherapy agents are now standard of care for patients with advanced-stage hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), resulting in improved overall survival. However, even with optimal systemic regimens, fewer than 40% of cases respond to treatment, presumably due to resistance mechanisms, including antidrug antibodies and acquired resistance related to alterations in the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME).

42708851.title: Histotripsy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: From Bench to Bedside.
42708851.authors: Luo S, Wei X, Lu X, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a leading cause of cancer mortality, with limited curative options. Histotripsy is a noninvasive focused ultrasound ablation technique that destroys tumors through acoustic cavitation rather than heat-based methods, offering an alternative to radiofrequency and microwave ablation.

42770820.title: How I Do It: Identifying Signs to Differentiate Uterine Sarcoma (Leiomyosarcoma) from Leiomyomas at MRI.
42770820.authors: Hindman N, Tong A, Huang K

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: The prevalence of uterine sarcoma, typically leiomyosarcoma, is greater than previously believed, with current data indicating a risk as high as one in 770 women undergoing surgery for presumed leiomyomas (uterine fibroids). Presurgical detection of uterine sarcoma is an important clinical concern for gynecologists and gynecologic oncologists worldwide.

42386984.title: ESR Essentials: pelvic floor imaging-practice recommendations by the European Society of Urogenital Radiology.
42386984.authors: Abdelatty MA, Stankiewicz A, Maccioni F, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: We detail the imaging features of anterior, middle, and posterior compartment disorders and highlight common pitfalls. Implementing these recommendations by adopting the suggested protocols and reporting approach in routine practice will help ensure consistent, clinically relevant pelvic floor assessments.

fig.cap: MRD images in a woman with pelvic organ prolapse (A) at rest and (B) during evacuation. Note the anterior bowing of the anterior abdominal wall muscles (arrows), confirming adequate patient effort. Evacuation was not repeated, as the initial attempt was diagnostic, given the evident global pelvic organ prolapse and associated abdominal wall muscle contraction

42252995.title: Updates on Imaging Assessment of Pancreatic Cancer for Determining Anatomic and Biologic Resectability.
42252995.authors: Lee SS, Kim DW, Lee W, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is a highly lethal malignancy. Imaging plays a pivotal role in the diagnosis and management of patients with PDAC, with treatment strategies largely guided by the tumor stage and resectability at initial diagnosis.

fig.cap: Pancreatic head cancer involving a replaced right hepatic artery arising from the superior mesenteric artery in a 77-year-old man. Axial arterial-phase CT images of two consecutive sections demonstrate a hypodense pancreatic head mass (arrowheads) abutting the replaced right hepatic artery (small arrows) arising from the superior mesenteric artery (large arrow) and traversing the portocaval space. Because the aberrant right or common hepatic arteries arising from the superior mesenteric artery typically course posterior to the pancreatic head, they are particularly susceptible to involvement by pancreatic head cancers.

42233891.title: Histotripsy for Liver Tumor Ablation and Beyond: AJR Expert Panel Narrative Review.
42233891.authors: Abi-Jaoudeh N, Ziemlewicz TJ, White S, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Histotripsy was cleared by the FDA for liver tumor ablation in October 2023. The technology uses short-duration high-amplitude low-duty-cycle ultrasound waves, converging these focally to cause tissue cavitation.

42417694.title: Serial Changes in Epicardial Adipose Tissue Attenuation Identify Residual Atherosclerotic Risk Independent of LDL Lowering: A Post Hoc Analysis of the CAUGHT-CAD Trial.
42417694.authors: Khanna S, Xu E, Soh CH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The association of serial changes in EAT attenuation with coronary plaque remodeling, independent of LDL-C lowering, supports a potential mechanistic role for EAT inflammation in residual plaque progression.

42307514.title: Integrated Coronary CT Angiography Assessment of Plaque Vulnerability and Clinical Outcomes: The Morphology-Inflammation-Burden (MIB) Score.
42307514.authors: Andreaggi S, Scalamera R, Kim S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: A coronary CTA-derived MIB score correlates with plaque vulnerability by intracoronary imaging and identifies patients at increased risk for adverse events. These findings support the value of coronary CTA for noninvasive risk stratification in clinical practice.

42886154.title: Calcium Density as a Marker of Coronary Plaque Stabilization in Primary Prevention: The CAUGHT-CAD Trial.
42886154.authors: Vasanthakumar SA, Nicholls SJ, Nerlekar N, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: In asymptomatic, intermediate-risk individuals, statin treatment was associated with a shift toward higher density calcium within coronary plaques, most marked with effective lowering of LDL-C.

42900033.title: Patient-Level Perivascular Adipose Tissue Density Aggregation and Plaque Progression: Plaque-Free vs Plaque-Adjacent Segments.
42900033.authors: Lee SE, Sung JM, Andreini D, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Changes in pRCA, whole-coronary, and plaque-free PVAT were each independently associated with total PV progression. For noncalcified PV progression, plaque-free PVAT change was the only significant measure.

42993105.title: CT-Based Deep Learning Assessment of Aortic Valve Fibrosis and Calcification: Development and Multicenter External Validation Against Experts, Histology, and Outcomes.
42993105.authors: Grodecki K, Manral N, Kwiecinski J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Deep learning enables rapid quantification of aortic valve fibrotic and calcific tissue from CTA, demonstrating excellent agreement with both expert CTA and histological assessments. Quantitative analysis of aortic tissue composition provides additional prognostic value for all-cause mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in multicenter external evaluation.

42993106.title: Characteristics and Thresholds of Coronary Lesions to Predict Acute Coronary Syndrome From Artificial Intelligence-Guided Coronary Computed Tomography Angiography.
42993106.authors: Bär S, Knuuti J, Saraste A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Future culprit lesions vs nonculprit lesions by AI-QCT demonstrated significantly higher plaque volumes and were nonobstructive in 40% to 70%. Thresholds of TPV ≥55 mm3 and NCPV ≥32 mm3 were derived to predict future culprit lesions and associated with increased rates of lesion-level and patient-level ACS in 2 independent cohorts.

43066668.title: Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife.
43066668.authors: García-Lunar I, Fuster V, Kofoed KF, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

42663364.title: Incremental Predictive Value of Deep Learning-Quantified Coronary Atherosclerotic Volume: A SCAPIS Cohort Analysis.
42663364.authors: Malmqvist J, Wang C, Bergström G, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Automated deep learning-quantified TPV improved prediction of first coronary events beyond SCORE2, coronary artery calcium score, and manually derived coronary CTA measurements, and identified even small plaque volumes associated with increased risk in a general population without established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

42470409.title: Association of Lipoprotein(a) With Coronary Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Events: Findings From the SCAPIS Cohort.
42470409.authors: Björnson E, Bergström G, Brinck J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The findings suggest that Lp(a) increases coronary event risk primarily by driving a higher burden of atherosclerosis and that high Lp(a) accounts for 5% to 10% of total coronary disease burden in the population. These results support broad Lp(a) measurements and the use of coronary imaging for risk stratification in individuals with high Lp(a).

42446466.title: Optimal Reclassification of Aortic Aneurysms: Cross-Sectional CT vs 2D Transthoracic Echocardiography.
42446466.authors: Abusafia M, Jadam S, Keen S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Indexed parameters, particularly CSAH, improve risk stratification beyond absolute diameters and highlight size-based differences in AA. CE-CTA-derived indices provide an individualized precision imaging-based approach to surgical decision-making.

42412030.title: Association of Hemodynamic Disease Severity and Distribution With Risk of Future Acute Coronary Syndrome.
42412030.authors: Yang S, Chung JW, Park SH, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Hemodynamic disease distribution, as measured by PPGCT, complements FFRCT in predicting ACS risk. The integration of hemodynamic disease patterns provides additional prognostic value beyond lumen and plaque characteristics, with hemodynamic focal disease emerging as an independent predictor and a potential therapeutic target for ACS prevention.

42225573.title: Opportunistic Assessment of Coronary Artery Calcium Volume and Density From Non-Electrocardiogram-Gated Chest CT Using Artificial Intelligence: Prognostic Implications in a Screening Cohort.
42225573.authors: Kim NY, Kim YH, Lee JE, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: CAC density derived from chest CT using automated AI quantification was independently and inversely associated with MACE, providing additional prognostic value when added to CAC volume.

fig.cap: Representative cases of CAC with high and low densities. A: High-volume-high-density CAC in a 65-year-old male, showing diffuse calcification from the left main to the left anterior descending artery (blue areas). The Agatston score was 2,978, CAC volume was 2,343 mm3, and density was 3.8. The participant did not experience MACE during the follow-up period of 3,291 days. B: High-volume-low-density CAC in a 70-year-old male, showing scattered calcifications in the left anterior descending artery, diagonal branch, ramus intermedius, and left circumflex artery (red areas). The Agatston score was 853, CAC volume was 967 mm3, and density was 2.6. The participant experienced MACE 3,156 days after the baseline CT scan. CAC = coronary artery calcium, MACE = major adverse cardiovascular events

42264632.title: CT-Based Risk Stratification of Coronary Obstruction During TAVR: Clinical Utility and a New Volumetric Parameter.
42264632.authors: Abdelhafez A, Lankisch N, Iannopollo G, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: A CT-based algorithm stratifies patients into 3 CO risk categories, though the decision for CP in clinical practice seems to incorporate additional clinical and procedural variables. Although CP reduces CO risk, its efficacy is limited in patients with very small VTCV, which can be predicted preprocedurally via CT.

42333976.title: Standardized MRI-Based Quantification of Epicardial Adipose Tissue Volume: Reproducibility and Agreement With Cardiac Computed Tomography.
42333976.journal_full: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
42333976.authors: Gronwald J, Gersch SS, Böttiger Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Data conclusion
conclusion.text: The standardized MRI-based approach enabled highly reproducible EATV measurements with excellent repeatability. Agreement with CT was moderate, with systematically higher values on MRI, limiting direct comparability.

fig.cap: Representative visualization of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) highlighted in pink and surrounding pericardial adipose tissue (PAT) highlighted in blue in both cardiac computed tomography (CT) and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). LA, Left atrium; LV, Left ventricle; RA, Right atrium; RV, Right ventricle.

42861496.title: Development and Validation of a Coronary Artery Calcium Volume and Density Score.
42861496.authors: Bhatia HS, Razavi AC, Dardari Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: The CAC volume and density score, which adjusts CAC volume downward for higher density, and can be calculated from existing CAC reports, significantly improves risk discrimination and reclassification compared with the Agatston score.

42899353.title: Deep Learning-Based 3D CT Body Composition Is Associated With Mortality in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
42899353.authors: Hadzic I, Brendel JM, Mayrhofer T, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Automated 3-dimensional CT-derived body composition measures provide independent prognostic information and improve risk stratification for mortality after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Low subcutaneous adipose tissue volume and higher adipose tissue attenuation identify patients at increased risk, whereas higher skeletal muscle volume and attenuation are associated with lower mortality.

42948875.title: Multimodality Imaging for Left Atrial Appendage Closure: Practical Guidance Across Preprocedural, Intraprocedural, and Postprocedural Phases.
42948875.authors: Motairek I, Abadie B, Cremer PC, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Standardized device-related thrombus and peridevice leak classification and harmonized imaging protocols can enhance reproducibility and facilitate cross-center comparisons. Emerging technologies including computed tomography first workflows, 4-dimensional imaging, AI applications, and computational modeling further advance precision planning and surveillance.

43043987.title: Polarimetric Characterization of CCTA-Defined High-Risk Coronary Plaques: Linking Morphology to Fibrous Matrix Organization and Lipid Burden.
43043987.authors: Fujisawa N, Otsuka K, Jones GL, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: PS-OFDI-derived metrics were associated with CCTA-defined HRP features and conventional OFDI lipid parameters. Reduced birefringence in HRP lesions suggests altered collagen organization as a potential microstructural substrate underlying adverse plaque morphology identified by CCTA.

fig.cap: Angiographic, optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI), and polarization-sensitive (PS)-OFDI images show a representative coronary lesion with high-risk plaque in a patient with chronic coronary syndrome. A, Coronary angiography showing a lesion in the proximal left anterior descending artery (white arrow). B, Longitudinal coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) view of the same segment. C1 through C3, Cross-sectional CCTA images at the levels indicated in B by the color-coded arrows. D1 through D3, Corresponding structural OFDI images showing lipid-rich plaques. E1 through E3, Birefringence maps demonstrating reduced birefringence in the plaque region. F1 through F3, Depolarization maps showing elevated depolarization signals in lipid-rich areas. G, Depolarization-derived lipid core burden index chemogram summarizing lipid-related depolarization signals along the matched coronary segment. Color scales for birefringence (Δn) and depolarization are shown at the bottom right.

42446010.title: Comprehensive assessment of vasospastic angina using coronary computed tomography angiography: synergistic value of the presence of myocardial bridge, perivascular inflammation, and myocardial extracellular volume fraction.
42446010.authors: Sayama K, Kanaji Y, Usui E, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: A multi-parametric CCTA approach potentially identifies patients at high risk for VSA. The significant association of the transmural ECV gradient with VSA suggests that myocardial remodelling imaging provides a novel diagnostic window into the cumulative myocardial impact of vasospasm, independent of active adipose tissue inflammation and the presence of MB.

42644238.title: Coronary Inflammation Is Associated With Plaque Progression in Men With HIV.
42644238.authors: Nasrallah N, Atallah M, Lattouf C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Coronary inflammation, assessed by FAI, is independently associated with incident and progressive coronary plaque in men with HIV. These findings support a role for vascular inflammation in accelerated atherosclerosis in people with HIV and highlight FAI as a potential biomarker for risk stratification.

42488949.title: Pathology-Based Validation of Quantitative SPECT/CT in Patients With Suspected Transthyretin Amyloid Cardiomyopathy.
42488949.authors: Tersalvi G, Bois MC, Scott CG, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: In patients with suspected ATTR-CM undergoing 99mTc-pyrophosphate SPECT/CT, the Mayo 3D Score demonstrated superior diagnostic performance compared with planar metrics and comparable to SPECT Perugini, while correlating with myocardial ATTR burden and deposition patterns on pathology. These findings support its integration as a quantitative adjunct within clinical diagnostic ATTR-CM workflows.

42290203.title: Factors associated with aortic valve calcification in type 2 diabetes-a Steno INTEN-CT substudy.
42290203.authors: Haujir A, Kumarathurai P, Stidsen JV, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In individuals with T2D without cardiovascular disease, AVC is prevalent in nearly half of all individuals. Higher AVC was associated with T2D-related comorbidities, but not T2D severity.

42389791.title: Automated AI-Based Aortic Measurements From Attenuation Correction CT as an Adjunctive Cardiovascular Risk Biomarker: An International Multicenter Study.
42389791.authors: Marcinkiewicz AM, Shanbhag A, Chareonthaitawee P, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Artificial intelligence can unlock previously unused information within routine myocardial perfusion imaging CT attenuation correction scans by rapidly and automatically quantifying aortic size at scale. Opportunistic aortic measurements derived from CT attenuation correction may serve as an adjunctive risk biomarker and could add prognostic value to standard myocardial perfusion imaging without additional imaging or radiation.

42377128.title: Machine Learning Multiorgan Analysis of Coronary CT Angiography Body Composition, Myocardial Infarction, and Mortality in the SCOT-HEART Trial.
42377128.authors: Guimaraes AR, Williams SE, Macmillan MT, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Multiorgan body composition analysis using coronary CT angiography provided additional prognostic information, among which skeletal muscle attenuation was particularly important.

42262238.title: Sex-Specific Associations between Long-term Air Pollution Exposure and Coronary Atherosclerosis at Cardiac CT.
42262238.authors: Castillo F, Ladak AM, DesRoche C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Long-term exposure to PM2.5 and NO2 is independently associated with more advanced coronary atherosclerosis at cardiac CT, even at moderate contemporary exposure levels.

42301017.title: Hybrid Cardiac 68Ga-FAPI-4 PET/MRI in Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Feasibility and Pilot Study.
42301017.authors: Zhou Y, Lin H, Huang C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Hybrid cardiac 68Ga-FAPI-4 PET/MRI successfully enabled simultaneous molecular and structural imaging for nonischemic DCM.

42878809.title: The role of cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement in patients with acute cardiac symptoms and troponin elevation in the era of high-sensitivity assays.
42878809.authors: Vignale D, Gambato G, Palmisano A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In patients with acute symptoms, elevated troponin, and no AMI, a protocol combining CCTA + LIE/ECV enables etiologic assessment of coronary and myocardial conditions, refines working diagnosis, and entails a favorable prognosis when negative.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Patients with acute cardiac symptoms, troponin elevation, and no evidence of acute myocardial infarction represent a diagnostic challenge: cardiac CT with late iodine enhancement may have diagnostic and prognostic implications. Findings CT angiography with late iodine enhancement provided a diagnosis in 75% of patients and modified the working diagnosis in 48%. In the 25% CT-negative patients, no adverse events occurred at mid-term follow-up. Clinical relevance A CT protocol including coronary artery evaluation and myocardial tissue characterization may provide a rapid etiological diagnosis in patients with acute symptoms and troponin elevation, potentially supporting earlier clinical decision-making and reducing the need for additional downstream testing.

42982907.title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.
42982907.authors: An Z, Ma Z, Zhang M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.

42998158.title: Systolic pressure gradient across myocardial bridge mediates the effect of bridge depth on clinical symptoms.
42998158.authors: Sun W, Song M, Li J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: MB depth and ΔCT-FFRsys were independent risk factors for symptoms, and ΔCT-FFRsys appeared to mediate the morphological-clinical symptoms link. These findings suggested that integrated assessment, particularly ΔCT-FFRsys, might be a new non-invasive imaging biomarker for clinically identify symptomatic MB and understand its potential pathogenic mechanisms.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question The precise relationship between myocardial bridging morphological and functional features and clinical symptoms, and whether underlying key mediating factors exist, remains currently incompletely determined. Findings Depth, length, and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient of myocardial bridging independently predicted symptoms, with the gradient significantly mediating the relationship between morphology and clinical presentation. Clinical relevance Noninvasive assessment of depth and systolic trans-bridge pressure gradient can assist in identifying patients with symptomatic myocardial bridging, serving as potential imaging biomarkers and providing insights into the underlying pathophysiology of symptom presentation.

42763334.title: In vivo coronary stent evaluation using photon-counting computed tomography: diagnostic performance.
42763334.authors: Lacaita PG, Bilgeri V, Spitaler P, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Image quality of PCCT for coronary stent evaluation is improved compared to EID-CT, and the accuracy for detection of ISR ≥ 50% is high.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Does photon-counting CT improve the diagnostic accuracy for detection of in-stent restenosis (ISR) ≥ 50%, and image quality compared with energy-integrating detector (EID) CT? Findings Photon-counting CT provides higher image quality and a low rate of nondiagnostic stents (0.3%). For detecting ≥ 50% ISR, the diagnostic accuracy is high and the PPV is moderate. Clinical relevance Photon-counting computed tomography (PCCT) has the potential to overcome technical limitations of conventional energy-integrating CT in coronary stent assessment and could improve the reliability of non-invasive follow-up after percutaneous coronary intervention.

42230200.title: Per-vessel myocardial blood flow improvement after coronary artery bypass graft surgery quantified by CT myocardial perfusion imaging.
42230200.authors: Seresti A, Castillo E, Fahmy S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Our analyses suggest that postoperative perfusion improvement varies substantially between vessel territories and is primarily driven by the severity of baseline ischemia. Minimal improvement in territories without pre-existing hypoperfusion underscores the importance of per-vessel functional assessment to guide more effective revascularization strategies.

42618647.title: First performance test of a dual wide-coverage CT system.
42618647.authors: Zou Y, Tian J, Liu Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Clinical performance was further illustrated in a patient with a mean heart rate of 197 bpm, in whom CCTA acquired with this mode showed clear and sharp coronary arteries with minimal motion artifact at a radiation dose of 1.48 mSv. The dual wide-coverage CT system successfully integrates 16-cm wide z-axis coverage with high temporal resolution of the dual-source system, demonstrating potential for advanced dynamic cardiac imaging.

42314616.title: Beyond luminal stenosis: Epicardial adipose tissue volume reflects coronary plaque burden according to CAD-RADS 2.0.
42314616.authors: Meltem E, Rakıcı IT, Aric M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: EAV is associated with CAD presence, stenosis severity, and overall plaque burden, supporting its role as a complementary imaging biomarker of atherosclerotic burden on non-contrast cardiac CT.

42486966.title: Coronary plaque quantification on energy-integrating and photon-counting detector CT: reproducibility and power modeling for mixed-platform trials.
42486966.authors: Vecsey-Nagy M, Hagar MT, Osoria-Velasquez J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Quantitative coronary plaque volumes demonstrated high inter-scanner consistency between EID-CT and PCD-CT under optimized conditions. The dual-level power-modeling framework translates inter-scanner variability into actionable sample-size estimates for study design.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Quantitative coronary plaque volumes are increasingly used as surrogate biomarkers, yet variability between energy-integrating and photon-counting CT remains a major concern. Findings Harmonized reconstruction settings achieved high inter-scanner consistency with low variability when optimized reconstruction settings and automated plaque quantification are applied. Clinical relevance Standardized coronary plaque quantification across CT technologies enables reliable use of quantitative plaque endpoints, supporting mixed-platform longitudinal trials.

fig.cap: Representative example of lesion co-registration between PCD-CT and EID-CT. Curved multiplanar reformats show a predominantly calcified plaque along the left anterior descending artery. Three-dimensional vessel models (red, target vessel; blue, side branches) display automated lumen and wall detection; cyan markers indicate the proximal and distal lesion endpoints. The reference lesion was projected onto the paired reconstruction via closest-point mapping along registered centerlines, ensuring spatial alignment and consistent 3D mask placement across series. PCD, photon-counting detector; EID, energy-integrating detector

42470482.title: Growth-adjusted reference values for the main pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio derived from clinically indicated chest CT in children.
42470482.authors: Lyu Y, Yang M, Bu H, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The pediatric MPA/AA ratio is growth-dependent and should be interpreted against age-adjusted reference values rather than a fixed raw threshold. On clinically indicated CT, this approach may support more consistent interpretation while remaining complementary to invasive hemodynamic assessment.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question How should the pediatric main pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio be interpreted on CT when growth-related variation limits the use of fixed reference standards? Findings In 1306 children, the main pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta ratio declined with growth, and age-adjusted values remained associated with invasively defined pulmonary arterial pressure elevation. Clinical relevance Age-adjusted reference values provide a developmental context for pediatric main pulmonary artery-to-ascending aorta measurements on clinically indicated CT and support decisions on further hemodynamic evaluation.

fig.cap: Standardized measurement of the main pulmonary artery (MPA) and ascending aorta (AA) on contrast-enhanced CT. Axial contrast-enhanced CT image at the level of the pulmonary artery bifurcation. The MPA diameter is measured as the maximal short-axis diameter perpendicular to the vessel’s long axis. The AA diameter is measured on the same section at its widest luminal extent. Thin-section images and mediastinal window settings are used, including only the contrast-opacified lumen

42847821.title: The Effect of Different Gadolinium Delivery Rates on Objective and Subjective Image Quality in Cardiac Perfusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging.
42847821.authors: Mihl C, Pernot JC, Winkens B, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Higher GBCA injection rates resulted in higher blood-pool peak enhancement, yet did not translate into significant differences in objective image and subjective image quality. Lower injection rates appear sufficient to achieve adequate myocardial perfusion imaging, suggesting a plateau in image quality in which increasing flow rates do not show added benefit.

42860780.title: Improved Visualization of Heart Valves With 4D-CT Using a Novel Motion Correction Algorithm.
42860780.authors: Zedler D, Demmert TT, Ritter A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: A novel motion correction algorithm substantially reduced motion artifacts and improved image quality in both native and prosthetic heart valve imaging with PCD-CT, with the largest improvements in systole. These benefits resulted in enhanced visualization of valvular pathology, potentially reinforcing the growing clinical role of cardiac CT for the assessment of valve disease.

43034193.title: Carotid CTA with automated plaque quantification for risk stratification of coexisting obstructive coronary artery disease.
43034193.authors: Xu L, Zhao M, Zhou C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In this retrospective study, automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA provides an adjunctive risk stratification tool to identify patients at high risk for coexisting OCAD, potentially guiding decisions regarding downstream coronary examinations.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Quantitative analysis of carotid plaque components on CTA may help identify patients with OCAD. Findings A model integrating automated carotid plaque volumes and clinical factors effectively identified OCAD. Clinical Relevance This study demonstrates that automated carotid plaque quantification on CTA may serve as an adjunctive risk stratification tool to guide downstream coronary testing in patients with cerebrovascular disease.

43055828.title: Diagnostic performance of dual-phase photon-counting detector for localization of parathyroid adenomas after inconclusive first-line imaging.
43055828.authors: Rau S, Rau A, Agarwal P, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Dual-phase PCD-CT provided reader-dependent parathyroid localization at low radiation dose in a difficult second-line cohort. Quantitative wash-out may aid differentiation from thyroid and lymph-node mimics but requires prospective threshold validation.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Inconclusive first-line imaging complicates parathyroid lesion localization. Findings Reader sensitivity ranged from 67.3% to 83.7% at 1.23 mSv.

fig.cap: Multiple parathyroid adenomas on FECh PET/CT and dual-phase PCD-CT. Images from a patient with biochemically confirmed pHPT, a history of urolithiasis, and an inconclusive cervical ultrasound examination. Representative images show two histologically confirmed parathyroid adenomas. One adenoma is located orthotopically caudally, to the right of the thyroid gland (arrowhead), and one adenoma is located ectopically, paraesophageally (arrow). The images on the left (a) show the FECh PET scan, with two focal uptake spots corresponding to the adenomas, each with a suspected anatomical correlate in the axial slice from the non-contrast CT scan. The axial slice from the arterial (b) and portal-venous (c) contrast-enhanced dual-phase PCD-CT shows a clear enhancement of the lesions, particularly at 40 keV in the arterial phase, with a visually apparent washout in the venous phase, here best seen in the 70 keV images. PCD-CT, photon-counting detector CT; VNC, virtual non contrast; FECh, [18F]fluoroethylcholine

42697979.title: High-pitch free-breathing triple rule-out CT angiography for acute chest pain: a prospective sequential two-cohort comparison of radiation dose and diagnostic image quality.
42697979.authors: Yu J, Peng Z, Yu X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: High-pitch free-breathing TRO-CTA substantially reduces radiation dose while preserving comparable diagnostic image quality, offering a clinically feasible low-dose alternative to standard breath-hold protocols for emergency patients with acute chest pain, particularly those with well-controlled heart rates.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question: Conventional TRO-CTA involves high radiation exposure (8.93-17.5 mSv) and breath-holding, posing safety and feasibility challenges in emergency patients with acute chest pain.

fig.cap: A patient who presented with acute chest pain and dyspnea underwent TRO-CTA using a high-pitch protocol on a third-generation dual-source CT system. a–c Curved planar reconstruction of coronary arteries showing no plaques or stenosis in the left anterior descending artery (a), the left circumflex artery (b), and the right CA (c). d–f PE in the segmental and subsegmental arteries of both lungs. Three-dimensional volume rendering (d) with emboli shown in purple, coronal maximum intensity projection (e), and pulmonary arterial maximum intensity projection (f). g–i No motion artifacts or indications of dissection in the ascending or descending TA

42601523.title: Optimizing coronary CT angiography in patients with delayed contrast arrival using a free-breathing, high-threshold bolus-tracking protocol.
42601523.authors: Zhang Y, Wang Y, Li J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The free-breathing, high-threshold bolus-tracking CCTA protocol improves enhancement uniformity and facilitates optimal scan-phase acquisition in patients with delayed contrast arrival, providing a more reliable and patient-tolerant alternative to conventional breath-hold protocols.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Can a free-breathing high-threshold bolus-tracking strategy improve coronary enhancement timing and image quality in CCTA patients with delayed contrast arrival? Findings The modified protocol increased optimal-phase acquisitions, improved coronary enhancement uniformity, and maintained diagnostic image quality in patients with delayed contrast transit.

fig.cap: Coronary CTA images from matched cases across the four study groups. A VR and CPR image from a 50-year-old man (heart rate: 68 bpm; BMI: 30 kg/m²) in Group A (conventional–normal Tarr), showing mixed plaque with moderate stenosis in the LAD artery, calcified plaque with mild stenosis in the LCX artery, and mixed plaque with severe stenosis in the left posterior descending artery (L-PDA). B VR and CPR images from a 63-year-old man (heart rate: 58 bpm; BMI: 29 kg/m²) in Group B (conventional–delayed Tarr), showing mixed and calcified plaques with moderate stenosis in the LAD, calcified plaque with moderate stenosis in the LCX, and mixed plaque with severe stenosis in the RCA. C VR and CPR images from a 50-year-old man (heart rate: 60 bpm; BMI: 30 kg/m²) in Group C (modified–normal Tarr), demonstrating mixed plaque with severe stenosis in both the LAD and LCX, and mixed plaque with moderate stenosis in the RCA. D VR and CPR images from a 66-year-old man (heart rate: 59 bpm; BMI: 28 kg/m²) in Group D (modified–delayed Tarr), showing mixed and calcified plaques with severe stenosis involving the LAD, LCX, and RCA. Arrows indicate the locations of coronary plaques in each image

43083529.title: Beyond Calcium: CT Phenotyping of Fibrocalcific Aortic Stenosis.
43083529.authors: Khanna S, Zuhair Kassem T, Khaing PH, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Aortic stenosis is characterized by progressive fibrocalcific remodeling driven by inflammation, fibrosis, and calcification. Although echocardiography and noncontrast computed tomographic calcium scoring (aortic valve calcium score) remain the clinical standards for hemodynamic and structural assessment, computed tomographic angiography, already routinely performed for transcatheter aortic valve replacement planning, provides complementary tissue-level characterization of fibrotic and calcific valve remodeling.

42479005.title: Comparison of Photon-Counting and Energy-Integrating Computed Coronary Tomography Angiography for Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
42479005.authors: Kurugalage R, Bhatia A, Mukherjee A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusions
conclusion.text: Compared against conventional EID-CT, PCD-CT was associated with down-classification of stenosis severity, translating to fewer referrals for ICA and a greater rate of revascularization when angiography is undertaken.

42332979.title: Indications, protocols, and interpretation of cardiovascular imaging for the evaluation and management of athletes. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the European Association of Preventive Cardiology (EAPC) and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging (EACVI) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC). Part 2-Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance, Cardiac CT and Nuclear Imaging.
42332979.authors: Maestrini V, Gati S, D'Ascenzi F, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: The number of individuals engaging in sports continues to rise, and identifying those with cardiac substrates associated with increased risk of exercise-related adverse events is crucial. Athlete evaluation requires a refined diagnostic strategy to distinguish physiological cardiac remodelling from pathology.

42808160.title: Cardiac Imaging in Structural Valve Clinical Trials: Secondary Mitral Regurgitation.
42808160.authors: Chehab O, Capasso R, Delgado V, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Transcatheter mitral valve interventions including transcatheter edge-to-edge repair and transcatheter mitral valve replacement have emerged as vital therapies for secondary mitral regurgitation (SMR) in patients at high or prohibitive surgical risk. Advanced multimodality imaging is central to patient selection, procedural guidance, and outcome assessment.

42275241.title: Factors Affecting Contrast Enhancement on CT Images.
42275241.journal_full: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
42275241.authors: Alyani Nezhad Z, Toia GV, Rose SD, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: CT scans use iodinated contrast media (ICM) to increase enhancement of soft-tissue structures. Some techniques, such as CT angiography, accentuate specific anatomy.

42993301.title: CT and MRI in periprocedural transcatheter mitral valve replacement: expert recommendations by the European Society of Cardiovascular Radiology (ESCR) and the North American Society for Cardiovascular Imaging (NASCI).
42993301.authors: Palmisano A, Francone M, Rajiah P, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a minimally invasive treatment option for symptomatic patients with severe mitral valve disease who are at high surgical risk or ineligible for open-heart surgery. The procedure has been associated with improved quality of life and functional status in selected patients and is increasingly recognized as a valuable therapeutic option in the management of complex mitral valve disorders.

43034255.title: Comprehensive reporting of acute aortic syndromes: a practical approach for radiologists.
43034255.authors: Dessouky R, Shabaan RRA, Abdul Rahman AAE, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic pathologies with high morbidity and mortality. In the emergency setting, an accurate diagnosis is usually achieved by aortic computed tomography angiography (CTA).

42521849.title: Pericoronary fat radiomics on coronary CT angiography for predicting major adverse cardiac events: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
42521849.authors: Mirzohreh ST, Dehghan M, Sadeghi S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: PCAT radiomics derived from CCTA shows moderate predictive performance for MACE in patients with coronary artery disease and may provide incremental value over conventional clinical and imaging models. Standardized radiomics pipelines and multicenter prospective validation are required for clinical translation.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Can quantitative analysis of pericoronary adipose tissue on coronary computed tomography angiography improve the prediction of major adverse cardiac events beyond clinical risk factors? Findings Radiomics models showed higher AUC than clinical and imaging models, while combined models demonstrated the highest predictive performance across included studies. Clinical relevance Pericoronary adipose tissue radiomics may provide additional quantitative information on coronary inflammation and may offer potential incremental value for risk prediction in patients undergoing coronary computed tomography angiography. However, further external validation and standardization are required before clinical implementation.

42864584.title: Colour maps for representation of quantitative metrics in radiology: meaningful or misleading?
42864584.authors: Sollmann N, Wetscherek MT, Wichtmann BD, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: The increased utility of quantitative metrics in medical imaging has prompted the use of colour representation of the data. Colour schemes for image display can highlight pathology and distinguish normal anatomy, thus potentially aiding image interpretation.

fig.cap: Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) in a patient with high-grade glioma as displayed on axial standard T2-weighted imaging (A) and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (B), with DTI showing directional colour coding of white matter tracts (C). According to directionally encoded colour, red, green, and blue (R/G/B) depict a principal direction (left–right, anterior–posterior, and superior–inferior), and the tumour seems to compress and disrupt white matter tracts (C)

42683639.title: Clinical Applications of Artificial Intelligence in Cardiac CT: From Coronary CT Angiography to CT-Derived Fractional Flow Reserve and Myocardial Perfusion Imaging.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly transformed cardiac CT, extending its clinical utility from coronary CT angiography (CCTA) to CT myocardial perfusion imaging (CT-MPI). This review outlines the current advances in and future perspectives on AI-aided cardiac CT across anatomical, functional, and prognostic dimensions.

fig.cap: AI-assisted CCTA for plaque quantification and CT-FFR assessment. Representative images of a 55-year-old male patient with atypical chest pain who underwent AI-assisted CCTA. A: Automated CACS on non-contrast CT with a total Agatston score of 0. B: Curved planar reconstruction of the LAD artery by AI identified a noncalcified plaque in the proximal LAD artery (moderate stenosis, 53%). The insets show the cross-sectional, color-coded quantification of plaque composition at the selected plaque cross-section, including lipid-rich, lipid-fiber, and fibrotic areas. C: Three-dimensional coronary model with a CT-FFR overlay. The CT-FFR measured 1 cm distal to the proximal LAD lesion was 0.81. AI = artificial intelligence, CCTA = coronary CT angiography, CT-FFR = CT-derived fractional flow reserve, CACS = coronary artery calcium scoring, LAD = left anterior descending, LM = left main, LCX = left circumflex, RCA = right coronary artery

42690965.title: Lung Cancer Screening: Beyond Pulmonary Nodules.
42690965.journal_full: Radiographics : a review publication of the Radiological Society of North America, Inc
42690965.authors: Singh A, El Khoury T, Tannoury E, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Low-dose CT lung cancer screening reduces lung cancer mortality in individuals at high risk and frequently reveals clinically relevant incidental findings. In the National Lung Screening Trial, approximately one-third of screening CT examinations demonstrated abnormalities other than lung cancer, raising challenges related to interpretation, reporting, and further management.

42227858.title: Planimetric and Linear MRI Markers for Progressive Supranuclear Palsy Classification: A Large Multicohort International Study.
42227858.authors: Quattrone A, Bianco MG, Vescio B, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The DMPI and midbrain area performed well for differentiating PSP from other neurodegenerative parkinsonisms.

42301014.title: Genicular Artery Embolization Using Rapidly Resorbable Gelatin-based Microspheres for Osteoarthritis-related Knee Pain.
42301014.authors: Fleckenstein FN, David D, Garducci P, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: GAE using RRGMs is safe and is associated with clinically meaningful improvement in participants with OA-related knee pain.

42446361.title: Automation Bias in Action: Eye Tracking of Humans Reading Screening Mammograms with and without AI Prompts.
42446361.authors: Taib AG, Partridge GJW, Phillips P, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Incorrect AI suggestions influenced both reader accuracy and visual search behaviors during mammography interpretation. The greatest negative impact was observed with FN AI suggestions; therefore, AI thresholds should be calibrated accordingly.

42517763.title: A Decade of Change in Adult CT Radiation Doses: 2025 U.S. Diagnostic Reference Levels.
42517763.authors: Kanal KM, Frush DP, Gingold E, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: U.S. adult CT radiation doses have decreased substantially over the past decade. This acquisition-level, size-normalized methodology enables near-real-time generation of national DRLs and ADs for modern CT dose benchmarking.

42334348.title: Longitudinal Analysis of Changes in Deep Learning Image-based Breast Cancer Risk Scores over Time.
42334348.authors: Lehman CD, Mercaldo SF, Azam S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: AI-based risk scores from screening mammograms evolved over time and diverged between women who did and did not develop breast cancer, supporting their potential as dynamic biomarkers for risk-adaptive screening and prevention strategies.

42334350.title: Extending the PREVENT Equations with Cardiac MRI: Prediction of 10-year Heart Failure Risk.
42334350.authors: Zhu M, Dai Y, Pan Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Integrating cardiac MRI parameters into the PREVENT equations improved HF risk prediction and highlighted sex-specific pathophysiologic differences.

42334351.title: MR Lymphangiography for Diagnosis of Lower Extremity Lymphedema: Suppressing Venous Signal Interference Using Deep Learning.
42334351.authors: Ma J, Gong X, Zhang J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: LympClear suppressed venous signal at MR lymphangiography and improved image diagnostic quality in individuals with LEL.

42742385.title: Evaluating the Effect of Neighborhood-level Disadvantage on Brain Health: An Imaging Epidemiology Study.
42742385.authors: Willbrand EH, Stoeckl EM, Belden D, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Residence in the most disadvantaged neighborhoods was associated with adverse brain morphometry, including higher BAG, lower TBV, and higher WMHV at brain MRI.

42836750.title: Quantitative Chest CT-derived Fibrosis and Vascular Remodeling and Acute Exacerbation Risk in Mild Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis.
42836750.authors: Yang M, Kim S, Lee SM, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In mild IPF, fibrosis burden and vascular remodeling were associated with acute exacerbation risk, with venous and arterial remodeling mediating fibrosis effects, and higher small-artery volume fraction associated with reduced acute exacerbation risk.

42836756.title: Efficacy of US-guided Hydrodissection for Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: A Prospective Randomized Controlled Trial.
42836756.authors: Bose A, Tandon A, Mehrotra G, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: US-guided hydrodissection with NS alone resulted in sustained clinical and morphologic improvement in CTS, and the addition of corticosteroid provided no additional benefit.

42867370.title: Association of Disproportionately Enlarged Subarachnoid Space Hydrocephalus Features at MRI with Cognitive Decline.
42867370.authors: Saito K, Watanabe K, Ide S, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Incomplete DESH was more prevalent than complete DESH. Baseline THC was associated with subsequent cognitive decline.

42867375.title: Myocardial T1 Mapping at 3 T: A Comparison of MOLLI and ShMOLLI across Healthy Volunteers and Various Cardiovascular Pathologies.
42867375.authors: Zhang H, Cui C, Zhou W, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In participants who underwent 3-T cardiac MRI with both MOLLI and ShMOLLI sequences, native T1 was higher with MOLLI than ShMOLLI, but ECV was consistent across sequences.

42867376.title: Association of PET/CT Metabolic Parameters with Histologic Grade of Lung Adenocarcinoma: Implications for Surgical Decisions.
42867376.authors: Shen X, Shi H, Wan Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In patients who underwent PET/CT and complete resection for clinical stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, maximum standardized uptake value was an independent predictor of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma and helped identify high-risk patients treated with segmentectomy or limited nodal dissection.

42899936.title: No Reflow at Perfusion Imaging: Thresholds That Distinguish Functional and Tissue Outcome Groups in Acute Stroke.
42899936.authors: Xu T, Chen C, Manning NW, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: The presence of a lesion with DT longer than 4 seconds at 24-hour post-EVT perfusion imaging appeared to be the most informative candidate no-reflow definition.

42899937.title: Redistribution of Pulmonary Vascular Volume at Upright versus Supine CT.
42899937.authors: Ikeda O, Yamada Y, Yamada M, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Upright chest CT showed that, compared with the supine position, standing reduced TPVV, predominantly venous, with a vertical gradient, where dependent lower lung regions exhibited modest volume reduction.

42937536.title: Automated Opportunistic Bone Mineral Density Assessment at Low-Dose CT Lung Cancer Screening: Incident Vertebral Fractures and Mortality.
42937536.authors: Löffler MT, Rühling S, Sollmann N, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Fully automated opportunistic assessment of spinal vBMD predicted vertebral fracture risk and was associated with mortality in men after adjustment. Individuals with osteoporotic vBMD who heavily smoked had a 2-year fracture incidence above the 5% treatment threshold according to current osteoporosis guidelines.

42937538.title: Intended Thrombectomy for Basilar Artery Occlusion with Mild Deficits: Evidence from a Multicenter Prospective Registry.
42937538.authors: Qiu K, Hang Y, Ji J, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5.

42975301.title: Added Value of Preoperative Contrast Enhanced Mammography in Staging of Malignant Breast Lesions (PROCEM): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
42975301.authors: Gardfjell A, Rydén L, Niméus E, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: This trial did not meet its primary end point of a 10% treatment change; however, preoperative CEM improved malignant extent estimation.

42975303.title: Long-Term Comparison of US-guided Microwave Ablation Combined with Ethanol Injection versus Surgery for Nodular Retrosternal Goiter.
42975303.authors: Li YY, Zhang MB, Yan L, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: MWA combined with EI was as effective as surgery for nodular RSGs, providing comparable symptom relief while demonstrating fewer complications, offering a safer alternative for eligible patients.

42975305.title: Predicting Lymph Node Metastasis in Part-Solid Lung Adenocarcinomas with a Maximum Solid Portion Diameter of 30.0 mm.
42975305.authors: Li X, Ma J, Chen W, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Solid portion diameter had a superior diagnostic performance compared with CTR in predicting LN metastasis in patients with part-solid lung adenocarcinomas of solid portion diameter of 30.0 mm or less at CT.

42975307.title: Phase 2 Trial of 89Zr-Deferoxamine-Daratumumab for CD38-targeted Immuno-PET/CT Detection of Multiple Myeloma.
42975307.authors: Ulaner GA, Kuker RA, Diamond B, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In participants with MM, CD38-targeted 89Zr-DFO-daratumumab immuno-PET helped detect active myeloma in some participants with no signs of disease at 18F-FDG PET/CT.

43007080.title: Gadolinium Retention in Pediatric Bone: Linear versus Macrocyclic MRI Contrast Agents.
43007080.authors: Roberts DR, Moore RD, Harrison A, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Exposure to the linear agent gadobenate at MRI was associated with higher gadolinium concentrations in bone tissue than no GBCA exposure or exposure to the macrocyclic agent gadoterate; trace gadolinium in the bone tissue of controls may reflect environmental exposure.

43007081.title: Low-Dose CT Lung-RADS 2022 for the Management of Screening- and Non-Screening-detected Lung Cancer Associated with Cystic Airspaces.
43007081.authors: Mascalchi M, Cavigli E, Puliti D, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Lung cancer associated with CA accounted for 6.1% of screening-detected and 5.4% of non-screening-detected lung cancers. Outcomes were similar to those of noncystic non-small cell lung cancer, and Lung-RADS 2022 may facilitate earlier diagnosis.

43007083.title: Glandular Tissue Component at Preoperative Breast US and Recurrence Risk in Invasive Breast Cancer.
43007083.authors: Deng T, Moon WK, Yan C, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: High GTC at preoperative breast US was independently associated with an increased risk of ipsilateral or contralateral breast cancer after invasive breast cancer treatment, consistently across both institutions.

43007084.title: Comparison of 7-T and 3-T MRI for the Detection of Multiple Sclerosis Lesions.
43007084.authors: Liu X, Tian DC, Zhang Z, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Compared with 3-T MRI, 7-T MRI improved MS lesion detection across characteristic intracranial regions and key imaging biomarkers, with a higher proportion of CVS-positive lesions but similar PRL proportions, supporting the clinical value of 7-T MRI.

43043180.title: Temporal Trends in High-Risk Benign Breast Disease Detection at Screening Mammography: Results from the Breast Cancer Surveillance Consortium.
43043180.authors: Sprague BL, Ponzini M, Sattayapiwat O, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Over the past 2 decades, detection of atypical papillary lesions and radial sclerosing lesions increased, whereas detection of atypical ductal hyperplasia declined. DBT was associated with increased detection of high-risk BBD, including lobular carcinoma in situ, atypical lobular hyperplasia, and radial sclerosing lesions.

43043181.title: Endovascular Treatment versus Medical Management for Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion from 24 to 96 Hours.
43043181.authors: Yi T, Hong L, Lin X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Among Chinese patients with AIS due to LVO presenting 24-96 hours after symptom onset, EVT was associated with improved functional outcomes, without clear increases in mortality or symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage.

43043187.title: Quantitative CT Phenotypes and Prognosis in Combined Pulmonary Fibrosis and Emphysema.
43043187.authors: Wang H, Ni Y, Deng Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: Quantitative CT helped identify emphysema- and fibrosis-dominant CPFE phenotypes with different prognoses. The fibrosis-dominant phenotype was associated with higher all-cause mortality.

43076673.title: Hemorrhage Risk in Unruptured Brain Arteriovenous Malformations before and after Stereotactic Radiosurgery.
43076673.authors: Umekawa M, Shinya Y, Hasegawa H, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In patients with unruptured brain AVMs, SRS was associated with lower hemorrhage risk during the latency period when analyzed from the time of diagnosis.

43076675.title: Longitudinal MR Neurography Changes and Prognostic Significance of Hourglass-like Constrictions in Parsonage-Turner Syndrome.
43076675.authors: Tan ET, Turbin SE, Lin Y, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: HGCs persisted over the course of 1-year follow-up in PTS but were neither independently predictive of nor associated with muscle strength recovery. Muscle edema grades were associated with EMG denervation.

43076683.title: Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging and 2-year Neurodevelopmental Outcomes in Mild Neonatal Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy: A Multicenter Study.
43076683.authors: Liu X, Wang X, Zhao X, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: In neonates with mild HIE, a combined clinical and DKI model demonstrated higher discrimination for predicting 24-month neurodevelopmental outcomes than did clinical-only or imaging-only models.

42678255.title: Performance of Photon-counting CT for Assessing Pretreatment Breast Cancer: Comparison with Mammography, MRI, and 18F-FDG PET/CT.
42678255.authors: Fu Q, Zeng Y, Chang R, et al.

conclusion.label: Conclusion
conclusion.text: PCCT demonstrated similar performance to MRI for lesion characterization and detection of additional lesions, with better performance for nodal metastasis evaluation; however, detection of microcalcifications was limited.

42334355.title: Standardized Knee Meniscus MRI Reporting: An Interdisciplinary Delphi Consensus.
42334355.authors: Nguyen JC, Patel VS, Abrams GD, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Thirty-three panelists from 23 institutions participated in a three-round Delphi consensus process to establish interdisciplinary guidelines for reporting knee MRI findings on 11 meniscus topics: MRI criteria for tears, possible tears, tear patterns, tear descriptors, intrameniscal descriptors, meniscal roots, posteromedial meniscocapsular junction, meniscus extrusion, assessment of the postoperative meniscus, retear descriptors, and ancillary findings. All panelists completed all Delphi rounds.

42852923.title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance derived Myocardial Strain: Applications, Acquisition Techniques, Analysis, and Reporting. A Scientific Statement of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance, Radiological Society of North America, and European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging of the ESC.
42852923.authors: Gulsin GS, Ambale-Venkatesh B, Axel L, et al.

conclusion.label: Closing lines — abstract has no labeled conclusion
conclusion.text: Routine integration of CMR strain assessment in clinical practice has been hindered by the lack of agreement on imaging protocols and analysis methods, variability due to noise sensitivity, and a paucity of robust normative age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges. In recognition of the expanding applications of strain techniques in clinical and research CMR, this joint SCMR/RSNA/EACVI scientific statement integrates data from original research studies, guidelines, and opinions from experts across the field to guide responsible and evidence-based utilization of CMR strain.

42867374.title: Supplemental Breast Cancer Screening with Contrast-enhanced Mammography or Abbreviated MRI for Extremely Dense Breasts: The DENSE-2 Trial.
42867374.authors: van Grinsven SEL, Monninkhof EM, Mann RM, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Women with extremely dense breasts have an increased risk of breast cancer but also a decreased sensitivity of mammography. The Dense Tissue and Early Breast Neoplasm Screening (DENSE) trial, initiated in 2011, showed that supplemental full-protocol MRI screening reduced the number of interval cancers in women with extremely dense breasts.

42899941.title: How I Do It: An Imaging Approach and Review of Autoimmune Encephalitis.
42899941.authors: Pai V, Rutten C, Shroff M, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Encephalitis is a medical emergency characterized by inflammation of the brain parenchyma due to an infective cause or an immune-mediated process. Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) is characterized by a misdirected immune attack against neuronal structures, resulting in an inflammatory response.

42937535.title: Agentic AI Systems in Radiology: Design, Applications, Evaluation, and Challenges.
42937535.authors: Bluethgen C, Van Veen D, Truhn D, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Building agents that perceive and act on their environment with a degree of autonomy has long been a focus of artificial intelligence research. This pursuit has become far more practical with the emergence of large language models (LLMs) capable of using natural language to integrate information, follow instructions, and perform forms of reasoning and planning across a wide range of tasks.

42808894.title: Updated European Respiratory Society-American Thoracic Society (ERS-ATS) Classification of Interstitial Pneumonias: The Radiologic Perspective.
42808894.authors: Piciucchi S, Ryerson CJ, Johkoh T, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: This review aims to summarize the key features of the 2025 update of the European Respiratory Society-American Thoracic Society Classification of Interstitial Pneumonias from a radiologic perspective. It highlights the revised terminology, pattern definitions, and conceptual framework, which moves beyond the previous focus on idiopathic interstitial pneumonias toward a broader radiologic-pathologic pattern-based approach that includes both idiopathic and secondary causes.

42808900.title: How I Do It: Bringing Together a Multidisciplinary Radiology Green Team.
42808900.authors: Northrup BE, Brown MJ, Hernandez AM, et al.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Radiology is among the most energy- and resource-intensive areas of health care, creating both a responsibility and an opportunity to advance environmental sustainability. Establishing a structured, multidisciplinary Radiology Green Team provides a practical framework for coordinating, implementing, and measuring sustainable imaging practices across clinical operations.

42550023.title: How I Do It: Understanding and Leveraging Generative AI for Chest Radiology Reporting.
42550023.authors: Hong EK, Lee S, Nishino M

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) has introduced new possibilities for assisting radiologists in diagnostic interpretation and workflow, particularly through automated report generation. Chest radiography has emerged as a leading use case for generative AI due to its high clinical volume, its diagnostic complexity, and the availability of large public datasets.

42578789.title: Advanced MRI in Multiple Sclerosis: Clinical Translation of Imaging Biomarkers in the 2024 McDonald Criteria.

fig.cap: Time windows for diagnosis and therapeutic monitoring using α-syn PET imaging in Parkinson’s disease. Pathological changes, including α-syn aggregation, begin during the prodromal phase in lower brain stem regions and olfactory areas (Braak stage 1–2), prior to the onset of functional deficits and clinical symptoms. The pathology spreads to nigral and limbic areas during Braak stage 3–4, when first functional and motor deficits start. During Braak stage 5–6, the pathology spreads to neocortical regions and results in advanced disease, dementia and widespread dysfunction. A PET tracer capable of detecting α-syn aggregates during the prodromal stage could enable early and differential diagnosis. In later clinical stages of Parkinson’s disease, α-syn PET imaging could serve as a valuable tool for assessing therapeutic responses to treatments targeting α-syn pathology in the brain. 41484253.title: The effects of prostate volume and PI-RADS category on optimal PSA-density thresholds for biopsy decision-making.

conclusion.text: The optimal PSAd cut-offs for guiding biopsy decisions were 0.20 ng/mL² for PI-RADS 1-2 and 0.12 ng/mL² for PI-RADS 3. extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question The optimal PSA-density thresholds for biopsy decisions in PI-RADS 1-3 patients remain uncertain, and data on the impact of prostate volume on its performance are limited. Findings Optimal PSA-density thresholds were 0.20 ng/mL² for PI-RADS 1-2 and 0.12 ng/mL² for PI-RADS 3. Diagnostic performance of PSA-density decreased significantly in men with larger glands (≥ 60 mL). Clinical relevance PSA-density cut-offs of 0.20 (PI-RADS 1-2) and 0.12 ng/mL² (PI-RADS 3) can guide biopsy decisions. In PI-RADS 1-3 patients with large prostate (≥ 60 mL), PSA-density becomes significantly less predictive, and low values may not reliably exclude csPCa.

41610036.title: Enhanced Myometrial Vascularity: Is It an Arteriovenous Malformation? Review of Definitions, Imaging Findings, and Management.

conclusion.label: Abstract opening — no stated conclusion
conclusion.text: Enhanced myometrial vascularity (EMV) is a common postpregnancy (ie, postpartum, postpregnancy termination, and postpregnancy loss) sonographic finding that represents involuting myometrial hypervascularity of the placental bed in the early puerperium and may persist if retained products of conception (RPOC) are present. 41670023.title: Effect of colchicine on progression of known coronary atherosclerosis in patients with stable coronary artery disease: EKSTROM randomized placebo controlled trial.

Colchicine was well tolerated, with no major safety concerns. In this stable well-treated CAD population, LAP was rare and not significantly reduced; however, it slowed overall plaque progression, supporting further investigation of its role in secondary prevention of coronary artery disease.

41519628.title: Novel deep learning CCTA-FFR for detecting functionally significant coronary stenosis: Comparison with iFR.

extras.text: LLMs demonstrated strong potential in automating CAD-RADS 2.0-compliant structured reporting for CCTA. LLMs could significantly enhance efficiency in radiological reporting. LLMs need further optimization before clinical integration.

41781729.title: Artificial intelligence-based coronary computed tomography angiography quantification of atherosclerosis burden: comparison with intravascular ultrasound in the INVICTUS Registry.

extras.label: Key points
extras.text: Question Coronary atheroma burden is a powerful predictor of cardiovascular events. Can AI-based coronary CT angiography (CCTA) accurately quantify atherosclerotic burden across the full disease spectrum when compared with intravascular ultrasound (IVUS)? Findings AI-based CCTA quantification (AI-QCT) showed strong correlations with IVUS for plaque volume, burden, and calcium across whole coronary segments, including non-calcified and low-attenuation plaques. Clinical relevance AI-QCT provides rapid, automatic, and accurate atherosclerosis quantification without reader-dependent variability, enabling standardized cardiovascular risk assessment, treatment monitoring, and therapeutic decision-making across all disease severity spectrum in routine clinical practice.

extras.label: Critical relevance statement

extras.label: Key points

The fully automated approach provides a foundation for standardized and scalable CT image quality analysis in research and clinical practice.

fig.cap: Exemplary case of the segmentation of (right-sided) autochthonous back muscles of the original and modified BOA. This illustrates, using an exemplary case, the confounding factors identified in the segmentation process and how these were mitigated in the iterations of the modified BOA: arrow A in m_original points to an area of adjacent fat that was erroneously segmented, subtracted in m_minus_fat. In m_minus_fat, a fringe-like partial volume effect between the subtracted fat and the muscle is still segmented and is largely removed by m_erode2. Arrow B in m_minus_fat indicates individual subtracted fat-dense voxels, part of a delicate fat layer. In m_erode2-8, an erosion of the segmentation around these voxels is observed, removing adjacent hypodense but non-fat-dense voxels caused by a partial volume effect from the delicate intersecting fat layer

fig.cap: Improved assessment of dense calcified arteries. A: Axial oblique coronary CTA from an EID-CT scanner in a 71-year-old male shows dense calcified plaque in the proximal and mid left anterior descending coronary artery, resulting in severe stenosis. Calcium margins are poorly defined. B: Coronary CTA in the same patient from a PCCT scanner shows sharper plaque definition with reduced blooming, revealing moderate stenosis. By reducing blooming, PCCT enables more accurate estimation of luminal stenosis, which correlates more closely with invasive coronary angiography. C: Axial CTA in a 75-year-old male shows a heavily calcified popliteal artery with severe stenosis and marked calcium blooming on EID-CT (red circle). 39233112.title: Cardiac positron emission tomography and other modalities for coronary artery disease assessment: A snapshot from the medicare data.
